statement: The function returns a result r (it does not fail), and r = true if and only if there exist indices i, j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n such that matrix[i][j] = target.
preconditions: Let m = len(matrix) and n = len(matrix[0]). 1 <= m <= 300, 1 <= n <= 300, and len(matrix[i]) = n for every i with 0 <= i < m. For every i, j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n: -10^9 <= matrix[i][j] <= 10^9; if j + 1 < n then matrix[i][j] <= matrix[i][j+1] (rows are non-decreasing left to right); if i + 1 < m then matrix[i][j] <= matrix[i+1][j] (columns are non-decreasing top to bottom). Also -10^9 <= target <= 10^9.

statement: The function returns a result for every input satisfying the preconditions: it never fails, panics, accesses an out-of-bounds index, or performs overflow.
preconditions: Let m = len(matrix) and n = len(matrix[0]). 1 <= m <= 300, 1 <= n <= 300, and len(matrix[i]) = n for every i with 0 <= i < m. For every i, j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n: -10^9 <= matrix[i][j] <= 10^9; if j + 1 < n then matrix[i][j] <= matrix[i][j+1]; if i + 1 < m then matrix[i][j] <= matrix[i+1][j]. Also -10^9 <= target <= 10^9.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r = true, there exist indices i, j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n such that matrix[i][j] = target: every true answer is backed by an actual occurrence of target at a concrete position in the matrix.
preconditions: Let m = len(matrix) and n = len(matrix[0]). 1 <= m <= 300, 1 <= n <= 300, and len(matrix[i]) = n for every i with 0 <= i < m. For every i, j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n: -10^9 <= matrix[i][j] <= 10^9; if j + 1 < n then matrix[i][j] <= matrix[i][j+1]; if i + 1 < m then matrix[i][j] <= matrix[i+1][j]. Also -10^9 <= target <= 10^9.

statement: Whenever there exist indices i, j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n such that matrix[i][j] = target, the function returns a result r with r = true: every occurrence of target in the matrix forces a true answer.
preconditions: Let m = len(matrix) and n = len(matrix[0]). 1 <= m <= 300, 1 <= n <= 300, and len(matrix[i]) = n for every i with 0 <= i < m. For every i, j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n: -10^9 <= matrix[i][j] <= 10^9; if j + 1 < n then matrix[i][j] <= matrix[i][j+1]; if i + 1 < m then matrix[i][j] <= matrix[i+1][j]. Also -10^9 <= target <= 10^9.

statement: For every matrix T with len(T) = n, len(T[j]) = m for every j with 0 <= j < n, and T[j][i] = matrix[i][j] for all i with 0 <= i < m and all j with 0 <= j < n (so T is the transpose of matrix), whenever search_matrix(matrix, target) returns r, the call search_matrix(T, target) returns a result r' with r' = r.
preconditions: Let m = len(matrix) and n = len(matrix[0]). 1 <= m <= 300, 1 <= n <= 300, and len(matrix[i]) = n for every i with 0 <= i < m. For every i, j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n: -10^9 <= matrix[i][j] <= 10^9; if j + 1 < n then matrix[i][j] <= matrix[i][j+1]; if i + 1 < m then matrix[i][j] <= matrix[i+1][j]. Also -10^9 <= target <= 10^9.
